subject: Renewal: stepdown credits & granular banding for hosted API commits
messages:
From: Kevin Patel <kevin.patel@larkhealth.com>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 1 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Renewal discussion — smoothing tiers and credits

Hi Aisha,

Our renewal is coming up in mid-Dec and the execs have asked us to take a closer look at the commit bands you've proposed. Usage in Q3/Q4 has been spiky; we're worried a strict tiered commit will over-commit for the low months and lock us into high uplift if we ramp down.

Two asks from our side:
- Can Redwood propose a smoothing mechanism or "bridge tranche" for the first quarter of the renewal to avoid immediate true-ups?
- We'd like to understand any stepdown/rollback credit if we drop below the committed band mid-term.

Rough expected consumption for next 12 months: 400M tokens/mo average with potential burst to ~1.1B in product launches. Procurement (cc'd Sandra) will need clear pricing examples to take to finance.

Thanks,
Kevin
Head of Platform
Lark Health

From: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>
To: Kevin Patel <kevin.patel@larkhealth.com>
Cc: Sandra Liu <sandra.liu@larkhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 2 Nov 2026 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Renewal discussion — smoothing tiers and credits

Hi Kevin — thanks for the clear context and for including Sandra. Really appreciate the upfront detail on seasonality.

Short answers up front: yes, we can offer a short-term bridge tranche to smooth the start of the renewed term, and we can formalize a stepdown credit with defined bands so you don't get penalized for temporary contractions. I want to align internal partners on the exact mechanics (finance + AM).

I'll pull together a worked example with:
- a 3-month bridge tranche that sits above the contracted band and is charged at a blended pay-as-you-go kicker
- a stepdown credit schedule (e.g., 10% credit if consumption drops below 60% of committed band in any rolling quarter, 5% between 60-80%)
- an uplift cap for renewal (we can cap uplift to a single-year increase of 15% unless contractually agreed otherwise)

I'll loop in Ben (AM) and Marissa (finance) to run numbers and share a spreadsheet you can take to procurement. Expect a draft by EOD Wednesday.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Aisha Rahman <aisha_rahman@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kevin Patel <kevin.patel@larkhealth.com>, Sandra Liu <sandra.liu@larkhealth.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Nov 2026 15:20:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Renewal discussion — smoothing tiers and credits

Thanks Aisha — adding some detail from pricing/finance side.

Proposed structure (initial sketch):
- Commit bands (annualized tokens): Band A: 0-6B; Band B: 6B-18B; Band C: 18B+
- Per-token list pricing will be lower as you move bands; we'll offer per-token discounts at band thresholds.
- Bridge tranche: 3 months where overage is billed at list*0.85 (a temporary blended rate) and counts toward the next quarter true-up only up to 50% of the tranche. This avoids large one-off spikes translating into permanent higher commits.
- Stepdown credits: if rolling-quarter average falls below 60% of committed band, customer receives credit equal to 25% of the difference for that quarter, paid as invoice credit. 60-80% -> 10% credit. These are one-way (credits, not retroactive rate changes).
- Renewal uplift cap: 15% year-over-year CPI-like cap for per-token baseline. For customers scaling fast, we still allow re-pricing by mutual agreement.

Attached is a worked model (redwood-pricing-model-v4.xlsx) with three scenarios: conservative, base, and expansion.

Let me know which scenario matches Lark's plan and we'll convert to SOW language.

—Ben
Director, Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-pricing-model-v4.xlsx (pricing model, scenario tabs)

Ben/Aisha — this is helpful, thank you. A few clarifying questions from procurement & finance: 
1) For the bridge tranche, can you show an example where we open the term 30% above committed band for three months and how that flows into the blended charge vs. being absorbed into next quarter?
2) Stepdown credits — are those cash credits on the invoice or an account-level token credit? Need to confirm with our accounting team (GAAP implications).
3) The uplift cap of 15% — can this be contract language (firm) or is it an "intent" in the SOW?

From a scenario perspective, the conservative model is closest to our internal forecast but with occasional bursts up to your expansion scenario once a quarter. We'll send a short forecast to you by Friday.

Kevin

Subject: RE: Renewal discussion — smoothing tiers and credits

Kevin — thanks. Answers inline and attached a draft SOW excerpt and pricing workbook.

1) Bridge tranche example: see tab "BridgeExample" in the attached spreadsheet. Short summary: if you open 30% above committed band for months 1-3, 50% of that overage counts toward the following quarter's consumption for true-up (the remaining 50% is billed at blended list*0.85 and does not permanently raise your committed band). The net effect smooths month-to-month spikes while protecting long-term economics.

2) Stepdown credits: invoice credits (account-level credit memos). We designed them as billing credits to avoid GAAP revenue reclassification complexity on your end; happy to discuss with your accounting folks. Example: committed band = 6B tokens/yr (=0.5B/mo). If rolling-quarter average falls to 0.25B/mo (50%), Lark would receive a credit equal to 25% of the difference between billed consumption and the contracted band for that quarter.

3) Uplift cap: we can include a contractual clause that caps allowed year-over-year baseline rate increases to 15% unless both parties sign an amendment. That will appear in the SOW language.

Attached: redwood-pricing-model-v4.xlsx (worked scenarios + BridgeExample tab), Lark-SOW-draft.pdf (SOW excerpt with stepdown & uplift cap language).

Next steps:
- Kevin/Sandra: confirm which scenario to lock for the first 12 months (Conservative/Base/Expansion)
- Redwood: we'll produce final SOW and DocuSign package once scenario selected

Thanks — we can also run a short 30m walkthrough of the BridgeExample with finance next week if that helps.

Best,
Aisha Rahman
